voice: Reserved, precise, and quietly witty Egyptian accountant; educated, family-oriented, and passionate about cultural repatriation, with standard spelling and no exoticizing cliches.

entries.text: Thank you, Miss Bow, but I don't need that.
Yes, I would say so. Business is booming, and New York has no shortage of people in need of an accountant. My wife Isis is expecting our third child very soon. I have every reason to be content.
There's Horus and Amon, and the new baby will be Anubis. My wife and I settled on the name long ago.
Boy or girl, the name will be Anubis. We are quite decided.
The ankh is an Egyptian symbol of life. It remains sacred to many of our people.
I'm afraid I do not know Mr. Augustini. I live a quiet life and know very few famous people.
Bifocals? You seem rather young to need them, Miss Bow. I have been fortunate enough not to require them yet. Perhaps you should try reading in a brighter light.
I'm afraid I have no idea whose boot that may be, Miss Bow. I do very little manual labor myself. My lungs are rather weak.
No, but whoever stole it should face the full weight of the law--and perhaps a little more besides. Forgive me. The subject makes me uncharacteristically heated.
Yes. Accountants use carbon paper quite often. It is a very useful material.
I have heard a great deal about Mr. Carrington, but I do not know him well. We have spoken only once or twice. He seems cultured and charming.
Charcoal? It is rather unusual to find a lump of it lying in a museum during a fundraising fete. Perhaps the handyman dropped it.
American cheeses often seem sharper and oilier than those I prefer. Give me a mild white cheese or a little goat cheese. Cheddar, particularly moldy cheddar, does not agree with me.
The Countess is quite a colorful lady. She seems determined to enjoy life to the fullest. Just between us, I find her a little alarming.
She is simply too enthusiastic for my taste, I suppose.
Crodfollers? No, thank you. I try to limit my sugar. It has a disagreeable effect on me.
The Dagger of Amon Ra is more than a beautiful object. It belongs to Egypt, and its theft is a genuine national loss.
I don't know anything about that. I'm sorry.
Bones? Large ones? I know very little about bones of any size, Miss Bow. You should discuss them with Dr. Myklos.
The docks are very rough places, Miss Bow. I stay away from them, and I suggest you do the same. A young woman alone would attract precisely the wrong sort of attention.
Not professionally. I have always taken an interest in my country's history, particularly its ancient religions.
I do not know Mr. Leach well, but he seems a decent, hard-working man.
That is a lovely gown, Miss Bow. I have not seen one like it for several years.
Miss Bow! Could we turn the conversation to a less delicate subject, please?
Yes, I have noticed that Detective O'Riley eats grapes constantly. I prefer dates myself.
I find Mr. Heimlich most intimidating. He seems to enjoy looming over people.
Those are Egyptian hieroglyphs, Miss Bow--part of an ancient writing system. They are beautiful, are they not?
John Bow is your father? I have never had the pleasure of meeting him. I have never visited New Orleans; that much humidity does not agree with me.
I know very little about lanterns, Miss Bow. I do not believe in desecrating tombs, and I have never enjoyed spelunking.
I use a laundry near my office on Forty-Fourth Street. They do excellent work with linen.
Pardon my impertinence, Miss Bow, but is it not a little strange to carry a lightbulb on your person? Are you afraid of the dark?
I'm afraid I do not know the gentleman. I lead a rather solitary life with my little family.
How interesting--you carry a magnifier. I am quite nearsighted myself, after years spent examining tiny figures in account books.
I have never developed a taste for beef, Miss Bow.
The Leyendecker is a beautiful museum, Miss Bow, but beauty does not excuse the plundering of tombs or the public display of the dead and their personal possessions.
New York is a lucrative place for an accountant to establish himself, but I find the city itself rather large and frightening.
I see you carry a notebook. I carry one as well, in case a particularly interesting calculation occurs to me at an inconvenient moment.
Dr. Myklos is brilliant, though certainly a little strange. We all have our foibles, do we not, Miss Bow?
To be perfectly honest, I do not care for Mr. O'Riley. He sees no beauty in ancient Egypt, and he is rather blunt in his dealings with others. I suppose that comes with his profession.

Carter defiled the tombs of my ancestors for his own glory. He appears to care very little about what is right, provided the discovery bears his name. Conduct like that eventually carries its own punishment.
I am not interested in anything that belonged to that horrible man, Miss Bow.
What a fine pocket watch. I always carry a timepiece myself. An accountant should remain conscious of every passing minute.
No, I cannot say that I have. Then again, I am not particularly observant of other people's possessions. I tend to keep to myself.
The police have been useless. They will not uncover the thief; eventually, his own crimes will expose him.
How nice--a press pass. Reporting must require a great deal of energy, Miss Bow. I am not sociable enough for it. I shall remain with accounting.
Why, I am Rameses Najeer, Miss Bow. I am an accountant and the proud father of two and a half.
Red hairs? I know no one with red hair except Detective O'Riley and that young man, Steve Dorian.
No, I don't believe I have. How interesting. It must open something quite particular.
No, Miss Bow, I'm afraid I don't.
My wife Isis carries smelling salts. She has a delicate constitution and reaches for them whenever she is startled--which happens rather often in our building.
That is for handling snakes, is it not? A sensible device, though I hope never to require one.
I had always understood 'snake oil' to be an American expression for fraudulent medicine. This appears to be dismayingly literal.
I wouldn't know, Miss Bow. I am a family man and do not frequent such scandalous establishments.
Mr. Dorian is a remarkably robust young man. He must have been a very well-fed child.
I enjoy the Tribune very much, Miss Bow. I read the financial page every morning without fail.
Dr. Smith is a very intelligent man. We have become friends of late, and I always enjoy the company of a countryman.
Animal hairs? I know very little about animals or their hair, Miss Bow. Most animals make me sneeze uncontrollably.
I sometimes carry a water glass myself. Accountants have a regrettable habit of forgetting meals and water when the figures become interesting.
I would rather not hear the details of criminals' shocking deeds, Miss Bow. I am prone to nightmares.
I do not know him. I do not associate with such people.
I know very little about wire, Miss Bow. I am an accountant.
I do not own wire cutters, Miss Bow, and I cannot say who would. Perhaps Ernie Leach?
Could that be one of Miss Yvette's shoes? She always seems to wear high heels.
Miss Yvette is a charming and very friendly young woman. She seems genuinely interested in Egyptology. We once had a long discussion about tombs.
I do not know Ziggy well, but he makes me uneasy. There is something watchful in his expression. I met him briefly at the party and avoided him afterward.
I'm sorry, Miss Bow, but I would rather not discuss that.
We have already discussed that, Miss Bow. Let us move on to another subject.
No, thank you. I have my own.
Thank you, but I have plenty myself.
Forgive me, but I do not wish to get my hands dirty.
No, thank you. I do not care for sharp cheeses, and the mold would irritate my allergies.
The real Dagger! Miss Bow, you must entrust it to the police before it is stolen again.
Please, Miss Bow. I am a married man!
Miss Bow, please! You are embarrassing me.
That is very gracious of you, Miss Bow, but I am not hungry at the moment.
My goodness, what a large lantern. Very practical, I suppose.
I do not need it, Miss Bow. I am already illuminated.
Please do not scrutinize me so closely, Miss Bow. You are making me nervous.
Please, Miss Bow, I am already feeling a little queasy.
It is most beautiful, Miss Bow. You must return it to its rightful owner. I am sure he would be most grateful.
No, thank you. I have one of my own.
You Americans are rather strange. No, thank you.
My wife uses smelling salts, but I do not. Thank you anyway.
No, thank you. I have no occasion to catch snakes.
We occasionally find a mouse at home, Miss Bow, but snakes have never been a problem. Thank you anyway.
Good evening, Miss Bow.
I am Rameses Najeer, Miss Bow. Pleased to make your acquaintance.
Miss Bow, that is really rather repulsive.
No, thank you. I'm not thirsty at the moment.
I am not interested in that odious person, Miss Bow.
Be careful with those. They look dangerous.
No, thank you. I have no need for wire.
No offense, Miss Bow, but that is disgusting.
Miss Bow, what would my wife say?
I have heard a great deal about Mr. Carrington, though we spoke only once or twice. He seemed cultured and charming.
No! I spoke with him briefly at the party. Tell me it is not true.
Yes, it is true. Someone impaled his body on a stuffed porcupine.
Shocking. Simply shocking.
It was not me, if that is what you mean. I would guess the murderer was the same person who stole the Dagger.
I cannot prove it, but the connection seems reasonable. Perhaps that nervous Ziggy fellow knew something.
I did not know Mr. Leach well, but he seemed a decent, hardworking fellow.
How terrible. The museum staff are dying one after another.
Not a thing, Miss Bow. I am only an accountant.
Carter defiled the tombs of my ancestors for his own glory. He cared very little about right and wrong when a discovery might bear his name. Conduct like that eventually brings consequences.
Oh...that is right. I had forgotten.
Hate is a strong word. We had an academic difference of opinion.
I sometimes become carried away, but it was merely a manner of speech.
I do not care for your attitude, young lady. You have a very suspicious nature.
Miss Delacroix is a charming and very friendly young woman.
No. What is the world coming to? One cannot spend a night in a museum without a murderer roaming the halls.
No. I did not know her very well.
I do not know when it happened, but I have spent the entire night in the basement.
I did not expect the Spanish Inquisition. You are not a police officer, so I refuse to answer any more questions about Miss Delacroix.
